findings.title: Team admins are incorrectly denied permission to add guests
findings.body: The authorization predicate requires a user to be both a team admin and a team owner (`isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...)`). These are distinct roles, so a normal team admin fails this check despite the feature/UI treating team admins or owners as authorized. Use `||` (or the existing team-admin-or-owner authorization helper) so either role can manage the booking.

findings.title: Guest blacklist can be bypassed with email casing
findings.body: Configured blacklist addresses are lowercased, but submitted guest addresses are compared without normalization. An address such as `Blocked@example.com` therefore does not match a `blocked@example.com` entry and is added/invited. Normalize submitted emails (and ideally existing-attendee comparisons) consistently before blacklist and duplicate checks.

findings.title: The endpoint accepts an unbounded number of guest addresses
findings.body: `guests` has no maximum length, while processing each address creates attendee rows, updates calendar attendees, and sends notifications to all attendees and organizers. Any authorized attendee can submit a very large array directly to this mutation and use a single booking to trigger mass email/calendar work and database writes. Impose a server-side maximum consistent with the product's guest limit before performing any writes.

findings.title: Attendees are persisted before calendar synchronization can fail
findings.body: The booking attendee rows are committed at lines 92-106 before `updateCalendarAttendees` is awaited. If the calendar update fails (for example due to an expired integration credential), the mutation returns an error but the guests remain in Cal.com without calendar updates or emails, leaving booking and calendar state inconsistent. Either make failure recoverable/retryable and report the persisted state, or arrange synchronization/outbox handling so the committed attendee change is eventually applied.

findings.title: Existing attendees can receive a duplicate scheduled email
findings.body: The notification call receives the original requested `guests` array rather than `uniqueGuests`, even though existing addresses are filtered out before insertion. `sendAddGuestsEmails` uses that list to decide who receives `AttendeeScheduledEmail`; thus a request containing one new address and an already-attending address sends the existing attendee a new-booking confirmation instead of the guest-added notification. Pass the actual inserted guest addresses (`uniqueGuests`) to the mailer.
